_comment: National organizations that publish chapter or group directories. These matter more than hospices for two reasons: they cover the loss types hospices don't (child, suicide, overdose, infant, military), and those are exactly our highest-intent, lowest-competition search pages.
_access_policy: Check each source's robots.txt and terms of service BEFORE writing an adapter. Where automated access is not clearly permitted, use the manual CSV path in scripts/ingest/import_csv.py instead. Several of these organizations would likely welcome a data-sharing conversation - asking costs one email and is the better first move for the large ones.

_status_key.unchecked: No robots.txt or ToS review yet. Run check_source_access.py.
_status_key.automate: robots.txt permits our paths; adapter may be written.
_status_key.manual_only: Automated access unclear or disallowed. Curate by hand.
_status_key.contact_first: Large enough that a data-sharing request should be sent before anything else.

sources.name: The Compassionate Friends
sources.notes: The authority on child loss. Highest-value single source we have - child loss is our best long-tail page and hospices barely serve it. Peer-led chapters, almost always free, usually monthly.

sources.name: American Foundation for Suicide Prevention
sources.notes: Well-maintained finder. Suicide loss is high-intent and almost unserved by hospices. Requires the crisis banner and careful copy - see the sensitivity rules in the verification policy.

sources.name: National Alliance for Children's Grief
sources.notes: The Dougy Center network. Nearly the only structured source for children's and teen grief support, which almost no directory covers well.

sources.name: Bereaved Parents of the USA
sources.notes: Complements Compassionate Friends. Expect overlap - dedupe on address and meeting time.

sources.name: GRASP (Grief Recovery After Substance Passing)
sources.notes: Overdose loss is badly underserved and carries heavy stigma, so people search privately rather than ask. High-intent, near-zero competition.

sources.name: Share Pregnancy & Infant Loss Support
sources.notes: Often hospital-affiliated, so cross-reference with health system pages.

sources.name: MISS Foundation
sources.notes: Founded in Arizona. Natural first outreach call - a local relationship is worth more than a scraped page, and they may share data directly.

sources.name: Soaring Spirits International
sources.notes: Widowed community, skews younger than hospice bereavement groups. Fills a real gap.

sources.name: TAPS (Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors)
sources.notes: Mostly national rather than local, but matters for San Diego and San Antonio.

sources.name: GriefShare
sources.notes: By far the largest network, but three cautions. (1) Volume would swamp everything else and unbalance our metro pages. (2) Christian and curriculum-based - must be tagged accurately so people who want secular support aren't misled. (3) Large enough that we should ask before taking anything. Deliberately last.
